Specifically: 1) several streaming calls that were ~120 tokens were billed up to the 1,000 token quantum, and 2) a handful of long-context hybrid sessions (one request containing multiple concatenated contexts) appear to have been bucketed separately instead of being aggregated into a single session.

This pushed us over the threshold for the next slab and created a ~12% unexpected increase relative to our projection. Can you help explain why those streaming calls were rounded the way they were, and whether there is room to adjust as a one-time correction while we update our telemetry?

I’ve attached the invoice and highlighted 3 line items (see PDF). We can provide logs if helpful — I’ve CC’d techops.

Subject: Fwd: Unexpected quantum rounding/minimums on May invoice — internal calc and proposed concession

Markus / Vanessa — forwarding Dana’s invoice question. Quick summary and my read:

- Line item A (streaming call) tokenized to ~120 tokens but was billed at 1,000-token quantum. From the logs (attached calc workbook) we see the request was a short streaming call that did not reuse KV cache — falls into the per-call minimum threshold and thus hit the 1k quantum due to our current per-call flooring rule.

- Lines B/C (long-context hybrid) appear to be two client-side stitched requests sent ~6s apart from the same session id. Our session-aggregation TTL is 5s (config), so they didn’t aggregate — borderline but technically outside the window.

Proposed remediation: 1) credit 75% of the overage for the streaming call (we’re flexible because this was the first month of the pilot and client telemetry is messy), and 2) for the two stitched requests, apply a one-time manual aggregation credit equal to the difference between per-call bucketed billing and the aggregated session billing. Net expected credit ~ $1,840.

I’ve attached a workbook (nova-quantum-calcs-2029-05.xlsx) showing the math and a sample tokenization trace. If you agree I’ll propose this back to Dana along with a brief explanation of the TTL behavior and next steps to avoid recurrence (increase client-side batching or extend session TTL via header).

Notes for discussion: are we comfortable offering a partial credit + process change instead of a full waiver? Also, do we mention this as a goodwill concession (no PR) or as a negotiated discount tied to next-quarter commit?

—Tessa

Hi Dana — thanks again for sending the invoice and callout. Appreciate the patience while we investigated. Summary of findings and remediation below.

What we found
- Streaming call (Invoice line A): tokenization was ~120 tokens and hit our per-call minimum quantum of 1,000 tokens under the current per-call billing rule because KV cache reuse was not present.
- Long-context stitched requests (Invoice lines B/C): two requests with the same session id were sent ~6s apart; our server-side aggregation TTL is 5s and therefore they were treated as separate sessions.

What we’re doing- One-time credit of $1,840 to adjust the two long-context items and a 75% credit on the streaming-call overage (net credit shown on a corrected invoice).- We’ve attached a short worksheet showing the calculation and the tokenization trace.- Operational recommendation: two options to avoid recurrence — (A) increase session TTL on your SDK calls by adding header X-RW-Session-TTL: 10, or (B) switch short streaming calls to a batched call pattern when output is small. We’re happy to help implement option A on a short call.

Next steps / mutual action plan
1) I will issue a corrected invoice showing the credit and updated balance by Monday, Jun 24.
2) Techops (cc) to decide whether they want the TTL header change (we can schedule a 30-minute runbook call).
3) If NovaCorp would like this formalized as a recurring concession tied to a future commit, we can discuss an amendment to the pilot terms.

Please let me know if this approach works and whether you want the corrected invoice pushed to your AP portal or as a credit memo.

Best,
